**William Howard Taft** (September 15, 1857–March 8, 1930) was the 27th [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") from 1909 to 1913 and the tenth [chief justice of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chief_justice_of_the_United_States "Chief justice of the United States") from 1921 to 1930. He is the only person to have held both offices.

Taft was born in [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati "Cincinnati"), Ohio. His father, [Alphonso Taft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphonso_Taft "Alphonso Taft"), was a [U.S. attorney general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._attorney_general "U.S. attorney general") and [secretary of war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_war "Secretary of war"). Taft attended [Yale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale "Yale") and joined [Skull and Bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull_and_Bones "Skull and Bones"), of which his father was a founding member. After becoming a lawyer, Taft was appointed a judge while still in his twenties. He continued a rapid rise, being named [solicitor general](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solicitor_General_of_the_United_States "Solicitor General of the United States") and a judge of the [Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixth_Circuit_Court_of_Appeals "Sixth Circuit Court of Appeals"). In 1901, President [William McKinley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_McKinley "William McKinley") appointed Taft [civilian governor of the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General_of_the_Philippines "Governor-General of the Philippines"). In 1904, President [Theodore Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt "Theodore Roosevelt") made him Secretary of War, and he became Roosevelt's hand-picked successor. Despite his personal ambition to become chief justice, Taft declined repeated offers of appointment to the [Supreme Court of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States"), believing his political work to be more important.

With Roosevelt's help, Taft had little opposition for the Republican nomination for president in 1908 and easily defeated [William Jennings Bryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Jennings_Bryan "William Jennings Bryan") for the presidency in that November's [election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1908_United_States_presidential_election "1908 United States presidential election"). As president, he [focused](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_U.S._foreign_policy#1893%E2%80%931914 "History of U.S. foreign policy") on East Asia more than European affairs and repeatedly intervened to prop up or remove Latin American governments. While Taft sought reductions to trade [tariffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tariff "Tariff"), the resulting bill was heavily influenced by special interests. His administration was filled with conflict between the Republican Party's conservative wing, with which Taft often sympathized, and its progressive wing, towards which Roosevelt increasingly gravitated. Controversies [over conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinchot%E2%80%93Ballinger_controversy "Pinchot–Ballinger controversy") and [antitrust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_antitrust_law "United States antitrust law") cases filed by the Taft administration served to further separate the two men. The [1912 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1912_United_States_presidential_election "1912 United States presidential election") was a three-way race, as Roosevelt challenged Taft for renomination. Taft used his control of the party machinery to gain a bare majority of delegates and Roosevelt bolted the party. The split left Taft with little chance of reelection, and he took only Utah and Vermont in his loss to Democratic nominee [Woodrow Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodrow_Wilson "Woodrow Wilson").

After leaving office, Taft returned to Yale as a professor, continuing his political activity and working against war through the [League to Enforce Peace](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_to_Enforce_Peace "League to Enforce Peace"). In 1921, President [Warren G. Harding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren_G._Harding "Warren G. Harding") appointed Taft chief justice, an office he had long sought. Chief Justice Taft was a conservative on business issues, and under him there were advances in individual rights. His work towards administrative reform of the court culminated in the [Judiciary Act of 1925](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judiciary_Act_of_1925 "Judiciary Act of 1925"). In poor health, he resigned in February 1930, and died the following month. He was buried at [Arlington National Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington_National_Cemetery "Arlington National Cemetery"), the first president and first Supreme Court justice to be interred there.

Taft is generally listed near the middle in [historians' rankings of U.S. presidents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_rankings_of_presidents_of_the_United_States "Historical rankings of presidents of the United States"); his work as chief justice has been evaluated more positively. In popular memory his political achievements and role in Republican Party history have been overshadowed by his weight and physical appearance.

## Early life and education

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/76/William_Howard_Taft_Yale_College_BA_1878.jpg/250px-William_Howard_Taft_Yale_College_BA_1878.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:William_Howard_Taft_Yale_College_BA_1878.jpg)

[Yale College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_College "Yale College") photograph of Taft, c. 1878

William Howard Taft was born September 15, 1857, in [Cincinnati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati "Cincinnati"), Ohio, to [Alphonso Taft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alphonso_Taft "Alphonso Taft") and [Louise Torrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louise_Taft "Louise Taft").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-ANB-3) The [Taft family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taft_family "Taft family") lived in the suburb of [Mount Auburn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Auburn_Historic_District "Mount Auburn Historic District"). Alphonso served as a judge and an ambassador, and was [U.S. Secretary of War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Secretary_of_War "U.S. Secretary of War") and [Attorney General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Attorney_General "United States Attorney General") under President [Ulysses S. Grant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulysses_S._Grant "Ulysses S. Grant").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie4%E2%80%935-4)

William Taft was not seen as brilliant as a child, but was a hard worker; his demanding parents pushed him and his four brothers toward success, tolerating nothing less. He attended [Woodward High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodward_Career_Technical_High_School "Woodward Career Technical High School") in Cincinnati. At [Yale College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yale_College "Yale College"), which he entered in 1874, the heavyset, jovial Taft was popular and an intramural heavyweight wrestling champion. One classmate said he succeeded through hard work rather than by being the smartest, and had integrity.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie4%E2%80%937-5)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-6) He was elected a member of [Skull and Bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull_and_Bones "Skull and Bones"), the Yale secret society co-founded by his father, one of three future presidents (with [George H. W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_H._W._Bush "George H. W. Bush") and [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush")) to be a member.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-7)

In 1878, Taft graduated second in his class of 121.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-NYTobit-8) He attended [Cincinnati Law School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cincinnati_Law_School "Cincinnati Law School"),[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie8-9) and graduated with a [Bachelor of Laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bachelor_of_Laws "Bachelor of Laws") in 1880. While in law school, he worked on _The Cincinnati Commercial_ newspaper,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-NYTobit-8) edited by [Murat Halstead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murat_Halstead "Murat Halstead"). Taft was assigned to cover the local courts, and also spent time [reading law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reading_law "Reading law") in his father's office; both activities gave him practical knowledge of the law that was not taught in class. Shortly before graduating from law school, Taft went to [Columbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbus,_Ohio "Columbus, Ohio") to take the [bar examination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_examination "Bar examination") and easily passed.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_149%E2%80%9353-10)

## Rise in government (1880–1908)

### Ohio lawyer and judge

After admission to the [Ohio bar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_examination_in_the_United_States "Bar examination in the United States"), Taft devoted himself to his job at the _Commercial_ full-time. Halstead was willing to take him on permanently at an increased salary if he would give up the law, but Taft declined. In October 1880, Taft was appointed assistant prosecutor for [Hamilton County, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamilton_County,_Ohio "Hamilton County, Ohio"), where Cincinnati is. He took office in January 1881. Taft served for a year as assistant prosecutor, trying his share of routine cases.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_154%E2%80%9355-11) He resigned in January 1882 after President [Chester A. Arthur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chester_A._Arthur "Chester A. Arthur") appointed him Collector of Internal Revenue for Ohio's First District, an area centered on Cincinnati.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_157%E2%80%9358-12) Taft refused to dismiss competent employees who were politically out of favor, and resigned effective in March 1883, writing to Arthur that he wished to begin private practice in Cincinnati.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie10%E2%80%9311-13) In 1884, Taft campaigned for the Republican candidate for president, Senator [James G. Blaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_G._Blaine "James G. Blaine") of Maine, who lost to Governor Grover Cleveland of New York.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_163%E2%80%9367-14)

In 1887, Taft, then aged 29, was appointed to a vacancy on the Superior Court of Cincinnati by Governor [Joseph B. Foraker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_B._Foraker "Joseph B. Foraker"). The appointment was good for just over a year, after which he would have to face the voters, and in April 1888, he sought election for the first of three times in his lifetime, the other two being for the presidency. He was elected to a full five-year term. Some two dozen of Taft's opinions as a state judge survive, the most significant being _Moores & Co. v. Bricklayers' Union No. 1_[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-15) (1889) if only because it was used against him when he ran for president in 1908. The case involved bricklayers who refused to work for any firm that dealt with a company called Parker Brothers, with which they were in dispute. Taft ruled that the union's action amounted to a [secondary boycott](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_boycott "Secondary boycott"), which was illegal.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_195%E2%80%93105-16)

It is not clear when Taft met [Helen Herron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helen_Herron_Taft "Helen Herron Taft") (often called Nellie), but it was no later than 1880, when she mentioned in her diary receiving an invitation to a party from him. By 1884, they were meeting regularly, and in 1885, after an initial rejection, she agreed to marry him. The wedding took place at the Herron home on June 19, 1886. William Taft remained devoted to his wife throughout their almost 44 years of marriage. Nellie Taft pushed her husband much as his parents had, and she could be very frank with her criticisms.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie13%E2%80%9315-17)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_180%E2%80%9381-18) The couple had three children, of whom the eldest, [Robert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_A._Taft "Robert A. Taft"), became a U.S. senator.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-ANB-3)

### Solicitor General

The death of Justice [Stanley Matthews](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanley_Matthews_(judge) "Stanley Matthews (judge)") created a vacancy on the [US Supreme Court](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_States "Supreme Court of the United States") in 1889, and Governor Foraker suggested President Harrison appoint Taft to fill it. Taft was 32 and his professional goal was always a seat on the Supreme Court. He actively sought the appointment, writing to Foraker to urge the governor to press his case, while stating to others it was unlikely he would get it. Instead, in 1890, Harrison appointed him [Solicitor General of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Solicitor_General_of_the_United_States "Solicitor General of the United States"). When Taft arrived in Washington in February 1890, the office had been vacant for two months, with the work piling up. He worked to eliminate the backlog, while simultaneously educating himself on federal law and procedure he had not needed as an Ohio state judge.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1106%E2%80%93111-19)

New York Senator [William M. Evarts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_M._Evarts "William M. Evarts"), a former [US Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State"), had been a classmate of Alphonso Taft at Yale.[[c]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-20) Evarts called to see his friend's son as soon as Taft took office, and William and Nellie Taft were launched into Washington society. Nellie Taft was ambitious for herself and her husband, and was annoyed when the people he socialized with most were mainly Supreme Court justices, rather than the arbiters of Washington society such as [Theodore Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theodore_Roosevelt "Theodore Roosevelt"), [John Hay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hay "John Hay"), [Henry Cabot Lodge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Cabot_Lodge "Henry Cabot Lodge"), and their wives.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1110%E2%80%93114-21)

In 1891, Taft introduced a new policy: [confession of error](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confession_of_error "Confession of error"), by which the U.S. government would concede a case in the Supreme Court that it had won in the court below, but which the solicitor general thought it should have lost. At Taft's request, the Supreme Court reversed a murder conviction that Taft said had been based on inadmissible evidence. The policy continues to this day.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTERosen_201827-22)

Although Taft was successful as Solicitor General, winning 15 of the 18 cases he argued before the Supreme Court,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-ANB-3) he was glad when in March 1891, the [United States Congress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Congress "United States Congress") created a new judgeship for each of the [United States Courts of Appeal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Courts_of_Appeal "United States Courts of Appeal"), and Harrison appointed him to the [Sixth Circuit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixth_Circuit "Sixth Circuit"), based in Cincinnati. In March 1892, Taft resigned as Solicitor General to resume his judicial career.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1120%E2%80%93123-23)

### Federal judge

Taft's [federal judgeship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_federal_judge "United States federal judge") was a lifetime appointment, and one from which promotion to the Supreme Court might come. Taft's older half-brother [Charles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Phelps_Taft "Charles Phelps Taft"), successful in business, supplemented Taft's government salary, allowing William and Nellie Taft and their family to live in comfort. Taft's duties involved hearing trials in the circuit, which included Ohio, Michigan, Kentucky, and Tennessee, and participating with Supreme Court Justice [John Marshall Harlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Marshall_Harlan "John Marshall Harlan"), the [circuit justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circuit_justice "Circuit justice"), and judges of the Sixth Circuit in hearing appeals. Taft spent these years, from 1892 to 1900, in personal and professional contentment.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie28%E2%80%9330-24)

According to historian Louis L. Gould, "while Taft shared the fears about social unrest that dominated the middle classes during the 1890s, he was not as conservative as his critics believed. He supported the right of labor to organize and strike, and he ruled against employers in several negligence cases."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-ANB-3) Among these was _Voight v. Baltimore & Ohio Southwestern Railway Co._[[d]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-25) Taft's decision for a worker injured in a railway accident violated the contemporary doctrine of [liberty of contract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liberty_of_contract "Liberty of contract"), and he was reversed by the Supreme Court.[[e]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-26) On the other hand, Taft's opinion in _[United States v. Addyston Pipe and Steel Co.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Addyston\_Pipe\_&\_Steel\_Co.\_v.\_United\_States "Addyston Pipe & Steel Co. v. United States")_[[f]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-27) was upheld unanimously by the high court.[[g]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-28) Taft's opinion, in which he held that a pipe manufacturers' association had violated the [Sherman Antitrust Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherman_Antitrust_Act "Sherman Antitrust Act"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie36%E2%80%9338-29) was described by [Henry Pringle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Pringle "Henry Pringle"), his biographer, as having "definitely and specifically revived" that legislation.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1143-30)

In 1896, Taft became dean and Professor of [Property](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Property_law "Property law") at his _alma mater_, Cincinnati Law School, a post that required him to prepare and give two hour-long lectures each week.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_197323-31) He was devoted to his law school, and was deeply committed to legal education, introducing the [case method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Case_method "Case method") to the curriculum.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1148-32) As a federal judge, Taft could not involve himself with politics, but followed it closely, remaining a Republican supporter. He watched with some disbelief as [the campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_McKinley_presidential_campaign,_1896 "William McKinley presidential campaign, 1896") of Ohio Governor [William McKinley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_McKinley "William McKinley") developed in 1894 and 1895, writing "I cannot find anybody in Washington who wants him".[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1148-32) By March 1896, Taft realized that McKinley would likely be nominated, and was lukewarm in his support. He landed solidly in McKinley's camp in July, after former [Nebraska](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nebraska "Nebraska")[US Representative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_House_of_Representatives "United States House of Representatives")[William Jennings Bryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Jennings_Bryan "William Jennings Bryan") stampeded the [1896 Democratic National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_Democratic_National_Convention "1896 Democratic National Convention") with his [Cross of Gold speech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross_of_Gold_speech "Cross of Gold speech") and was nominated. Bryan, in both that speech and in [his campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Jennings_Bryan_presidential_campaign,_1896 "William Jennings Bryan presidential campaign, 1896"), strongly advocated [free silver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_silver "Free silver"), a policy that Taft saw as economic radicalism. Taft feared that people would hoard gold in anticipation of a Bryan victory, but he could do nothing but worry. McKinley [was elected](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1896_United_States_presidential_election "1896 United States presidential election"); when a place on the Supreme Court opened in 1898, the only one under McKinley, the president named [Joseph McKenna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_McKenna "Joseph McKenna").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1150%E2%80%93153-33)

From the 1890s until his death, Taft played a major role in the international legal community. He was active in many organizations, was a leader in the worldwide [arbitration movement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arbitration#History "Arbitration"), and taught international law at the Yale Law School.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-34) Taft advocated the establishment of a world court of arbitration supported by an international police force and is considered a major proponent of "world peace through law" movement.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-35)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-36) One of the reasons for his bitter break with Roosevelt in 1910–12 was Roosevelt's insistence that arbitration was naïve and that only war could decide major international disputes.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-37)

### Philippine years

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Judge_William_Howard_Taft_and_the_Sultan_of_Sulu_Jamalul_Kiram_II_%281901%29.png/250px-Judge_William_Howard_Taft_and_the_Sultan_of_Sulu_Jamalul_Kiram_II_%281901%29.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_Taft_and_the_Sultan_of_Sulu_(1913).png)

[Sultan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sultan "Sultan")[Jamalul Kiram II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamalul_Kiram_II "Jamalul Kiram II") with William Howard Taft of the [Philippine Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taft_Commission "Taft Commission") in [Jolo, Sulu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jolo,_Sulu "Jolo, Sulu") (March 27, 1901)

In January 1900, Taft was called to Washington to meet with McKinley. Taft hoped a Supreme Court appointment was in the works, but instead McKinley wanted to place Taft on [the commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taft_Commission "Taft Commission") to organize a civilian government in the [Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippines "Philippines"). The appointment would require Taft's resignation from the bench; the president assured him that if he fulfilled this task, McKinley would appoint him to the next vacancy on the high court. Taft accepted on condition he was made head of the commission, with responsibility for success or failure; McKinley agreed, and Taft sailed for the islands in April 1900.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1159%E2%80%93162-38)

The American takeover meant the [Philippine Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Revolution "Philippine Revolution") bled into the [Philippine–American War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine%E2%80%93American_War "Philippine–American War"), as Filipinos fought for their independence, but U.S. forces, led by military governor General [Arthur MacArthur Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_MacArthur_Jr. "Arthur MacArthur Jr.")[[h]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-39) had the upper hand by 1900. MacArthur felt the commission was a nuisance, and their mission a quixotic attempt to impose self-government on a people unready for it. The general was forced to co-operate with Taft, as McKinley had given the commission control over the islands' military budget.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie41%E2%80%9342-40) The commission took executive power in the Philippines on September 1, 1900; on July 4, 1901, Taft became civilian [governor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor-General_of_the_Philippines "Governor-General of the Philippines"). MacArthur, until then the military governor, was relieved by General [Adna Chaffee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adna_Chaffee "Adna Chaffee"), who was designated only as commander of American forces.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie44-41) As Governor-General, Taft oversaw the final months of the primary phase of the Philippine–American War. He approved of General [James Franklin Bell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Franklin_Bell "James Franklin Bell")'s use of [concentration camps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concentration_camp "Concentration camp") in the provinces of [Batangas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batangas "Batangas") and [Laguna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laguna_(province) "Laguna (province)"),[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-42)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-43) and accepted the surrender of Filipino general [Miguel Malvar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miguel_Malvar "Miguel Malvar") on April 16, 1902.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-44)

Taft sought to make the Filipinos partners in a venture that would lead to their self-government; he saw independence as something decades off. Many Americans in the Philippines viewed the locals as racial inferiors, but Taft wrote soon before his arrival, "we propose to banish this idea from their minds".[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1174-45) Taft did not impose [racial segregation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Racial_segregation "Racial segregation") at official events, and treated the Filipinos as social equals.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1175-46) Nellie Taft recalled that "neither politics nor race should influence our hospitality in any way".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie50-47)

McKinley was [assassinated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_William_McKinley "Assassination of William McKinley") in September 1901, and was succeeded by Theodore Roosevelt. Taft and Roosevelt had first become friends around 1890 while Taft was Solicitor General and Roosevelt a member of the [United States Civil Service Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Civil_Service_Commission "United States Civil Service Commission"). Taft had, after McKinley's election, urged the appointment of Roosevelt as [Assistant Secretary of the Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_Secretary_of_the_Navy "Assistant Secretary of the Navy"), and watched as Roosevelt became a war hero, [Governor of New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governor_of_New_York "Governor of New York"), and [Vice President of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_States "Vice President of the United States"). They met again when Taft went to Washington in January 1902 to recuperate after two operations caused by an infection.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie52%E2%80%9355-48) There, Taft testified before the [Senate Committee on the Philippines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_the_Philippines "United States Senate Committee on the Philippines"). Taft wanted Filipino farmers to have a stake in the new government through land ownership, but much of the arable land was held by [Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic "Catholic")[religious orders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religious_order "Religious order") of mostly Spanish priests, which were often resented by the Filipinos. Roosevelt had Taft go to Rome to negotiate with [Pope Leo XIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_Leo_XIII "Pope Leo XIII"), to purchase the lands and to arrange the withdrawal of the Spanish priests, with Americans replacing them and training locals as clergy. Taft did not succeed in resolving these issues on his visit to Rome, but an agreement on both points was made in 1903.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurton_200435%E2%80%9337-49)

### Secretary of War

In late 1902, Taft had heard from Roosevelt that a seat on the Supreme Court would soon fall vacant on the resignation of Justice [George Shiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Shiras_Jr. "George Shiras Jr."), and Roosevelt desired that Taft fill it. Although this was Taft's professional goal, he refused as he felt his work as governor was not yet done.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1242%E2%80%93247-50) The following year, Roosevelt asked Taft to become [Secretary of War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_War "Secretary of War"). As the War Department administered the Philippines, Taft would remain responsible for the islands, and [Elihu Root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elihu_Root "Elihu Root"), the incumbent, was willing to postpone his departure until 1904, allowing Taft time to wrap up his work in Manila. After consulting with his family, Taft agreed, and sailed for the United States in December 1903.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1251%E2%80%93255-51)

[![Image 12](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Taft_crown_prince.jpeg/250px-Taft_crown_prince.jpeg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taft_crown_prince.jpeg)

Roosevelt introduces Taft as his crown prince: [_Puck_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puck_(magazine) "Puck (magazine)") magazine cover cartoon, 1906.

When Taft took office as [Secretary of War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_War "Secretary of War") in January 1904, he was not called upon to spend much time administering the army, which the president was content to do himself—Roosevelt wanted Taft as a [troubleshooter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Troubleshooting "Troubleshooting") in difficult situations, as a legal adviser, and to be able to give campaign speeches as he sought election in his own right. Taft strongly defended Roosevelt's record in his addresses, and wrote of the president's successful but strenuous efforts to gain election, "I would not run for president if you guaranteed the office. It is awful to be afraid of one's shadow."[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_19736%E2%80%937-52)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie64-53)

Between 1905 and 1907, Taft came to terms with the likelihood he would be the next Republican nominee for president, though he did not plan to actively campaign for it. When Justice [Henry Billings Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_Billings_Brown "Henry Billings Brown") resigned in 1906, Taft would not accept the seat although Roosevelt offered it, a position Taft held to when another seat opened in 1906.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie70%E2%80%9371-54)[Edith Roosevelt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edith_Roosevelt "Edith Roosevelt"), the [First Lady](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_Lady_of_the_United_States "First Lady of the United States"), disliked the growing closeness between the two men, feeling that they were too much alike and that the president did not gain much from the advice of someone who rarely contradicted him.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris380-55)

Alternatively, Taft wanted to be chief justice, and kept a close eye on the health of the aging incumbent, [Melville Fuller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melville_Fuller "Melville Fuller"), who turned 75 in 1908. Taft believed Fuller likely to live many years. Roosevelt had indicated he was likely to appoint Taft if the opportunity came to fill the court's center seat, but some considered Attorney General [Philander Knox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philander_Knox "Philander Knox") a better candidate. In any event, Fuller remained chief justice throughout Roosevelt's presidency.[[i]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-56)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1264%E2%80%93265-57)

Through the 1903 [separation of Panama from Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Separation_of_Panama_from_Colombia "Separation of Panama from Colombia") and the [Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hay%E2%80%93Bunau-Varilla_Treaty "Hay–Bunau-Varilla Treaty"), the United States had secured rights to build [a canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama_Canal "Panama Canal") in the [Isthmus of Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isthmus_of_Panama "Isthmus of Panama"). Legislation authorizing construction did not specify which government department would be responsible, and Roosevelt designated the Department of War. Taft journeyed to Panama in 1904, viewing the canal site and meeting with Panamanian officials. The [Isthmian Canal Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isthmian_Canal_Commission "Isthmian Canal Commission") had trouble keeping a chief engineer, and when in February 1907 [John F. Stevens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Stevens "John F. Stevens") submitted his resignation, Taft recommended an army engineer, [George W. Goethals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Goethals "George W. Goethals"). Under Goethals, the project moved ahead smoothly.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1279%E2%80%93283-58)

Another colony lost by Spain in 1898 was Cuba, but as freedom for Cuba had been a major purpose of the war, it was not annexed by the U.S., but was, after a period of occupation, given independence in 1902. Election fraud and corruption followed, as did factional conflict. In September 1906, President [Tomás Estrada Palma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom%C3%A1s_Estrada_Palma "Tomás Estrada Palma") asked for U.S. intervention. Taft traveled to Cuba with a small American force, and on September 29, 1906, under the terms of the [Cuban–American Treaty of Relations of 1903](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuban%E2%80%93American_Treaty_of_Relations_of_1903 "Cuban–American Treaty of Relations of 1903"), declared himself Provisional Governor of Cuba, a post he held for two weeks before being succeeded by [Charles Edward Magoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Edward_Magoon "Charles Edward Magoon"). In his time in Cuba, Taft worked to persuade Cubans that the U.S. intended stability, not occupation.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1305%E2%80%93310-59)

Taft remained involved in Philippine affairs. During Roosevelt's election campaign in 1904, he urged that Philippine agricultural products be admitted to the U.S. without duty. This caused growers of U.S. sugar and tobacco to complain to Roosevelt, who remonstrated with his Secretary of War. Taft expressed unwillingness to change his position, and threatened to resign;[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1261-60) Roosevelt hastily dropped the matter.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie67-61) Taft returned to the islands in 1905, leading a delegation of congressmen, and again in 1907, to open the first [Philippine Assembly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippine_Assembly "Philippine Assembly").[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1293%E2%80%93295,_301-62)

On both of his Philippine trips as Secretary of War, Taft went to Japan, and met with officials there.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMinger269,_274-63) The meeting in July 1905 came a month before the [Portsmouth Peace Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treaty_of_Portsmouth "Treaty of Portsmouth"), which would end the [Russo-Japanese War](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russo-Japanese_War "Russo-Japanese War") with the Treaty of Portsmouth. Taft met with Japanese prime minister [Katsura Tarō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katsura_Tar%C5%8D "Katsura Tarō"). After that meeting, the two signed [a memorandum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taft%E2%80%93Katsura_Agreement "Taft–Katsura Agreement"). It contained nothing new but instead reaffirmed official positions: Japan had no intention to invade the Philippines, and the U.S. that it did not object to [Japanese control of Korea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korea_under_Japanese_rule "Korea under Japanese rule").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMinger281%E2%80%93282-64) There were U.S. concerns about the number of Japanese laborers coming to the American West Coast, and during Taft's second visit, in September 1907, [Tadasu Hayashi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tadasu_Hayashi "Tadasu Hayashi"), the foreign minister, informally [agreed to issue fewer passports to them](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gentlemen's_Agreement_of_1907 "Gentlemen's Agreement of 1907").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMinger285,_291-65)

## Presidential election of 1908

See also: [1908 United States presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1908_United_States_presidential_election "1908 United States presidential election")

### Gaining the nomination

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/Wm_H_Taft_smiling_1908.jpg/250px-Wm_H_Taft_smiling_1908.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wm_H_Taft_smiling_1908.jpg)

One of a series of candid photographs known as the _Evolution of a Smile_, taken just after a formal portrait session, as Taft learned in a telephone call from Roosevelt of his nomination for president

Roosevelt had served almost three and a half years of McKinley's term. On the night of his own election in 1904, Roosevelt publicly declared that he would not run for reelection [in 1908](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1908_United_States_presidential_election "1908 United States presidential election"), a pledge he quickly regretted. But he felt bound by his word. Roosevelt believed Taft was his logical successor, although the War Secretary had initially been reluctant to run.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_197337-66) Roosevelt used his control of the party machinery to aid his heir apparent.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_197337-66) On pain of the loss of their jobs, political appointees were required to support Taft or remain silent.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1321%E2%80%93322-67)

A number of Republican politicians, such as [Treasury Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treasury_Secretary "Treasury Secretary")[George Cortelyou](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Cortelyou "George Cortelyou"), tested the waters for a run but chose to stay out. New York Governor [Charles Evans Hughes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Evans_Hughes "Charles Evans Hughes") ran, but when he made a major policy speech, Roosevelt the same day sent a special message to Congress warning in strong terms against [corporate corruption](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corporate_corruption "Corporate corruption"). The resulting coverage of the presidential message relegated Hughes to the back pages.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1337%E2%80%93338-68) Roosevelt reluctantly deterred repeated attempts to draft him for another term.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris523%E2%80%93526-69)

Assistant [Postmaster General](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postmaster_General_of_the_United_States "Postmaster General of the United States")[Frank H. Hitchcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_H._Hitchcock "Frank H. Hitchcock") resigned from his office in February 1908 to lead the Taft effort.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1347-70) In April, Taft made a speaking tour, traveling as far west as [Omaha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omaha "Omaha") before being recalled to straighten out a contested election in [Panama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panama "Panama"). He had no serious opposition at the [1908 Republican National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1908_Republican_National_Convention "1908 Republican National Convention") in Chicago in June, and gained a first-ballot victory. Yet Taft did not have things his own way: he had hoped his running mate would be a midwestern progressive like Iowa senator [Jonathan Dolliver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonathan_Dolliver "Jonathan Dolliver"), but instead the convention named Congressman [James S. Sherman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_S._Sherman "James S. Sherman") of New York, a conservative. Taft resigned as Secretary of War on June 30 to devote himself full-time to the campaign.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1348%E2%80%93353-71)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_197315-72)

### General election campaign

Taft's opponent in the general election was [William Jennings Bryan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Jennings_Bryan "William Jennings Bryan"), the Democratic nominee for the third time in four presidential elections. As many of Roosevelt's reforms stemmed from proposals by Bryan, the Democrat argued that he was the true heir to Roosevelt's mantle. Corporate contributions to federal political campaigns had been outlawed by the 1907 [Tillman Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tillman_Act "Tillman Act"), and Bryan proposed that contributions by officers and directors of corporations be similarly banned, or at least disclosed when made. Taft was only willing to see the contributions disclosed after the election, and tried to ensure that officers and directors of corporations litigating with the government were not among his contributors.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_197315%E2%80%9316-73)

[![Image 14](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f9/1908RepublicanPoster.png/250px-1908RepublicanPoster.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:1908RepublicanPoster.png)

1908 Taft/Sherman poster

Taft began the campaign on the wrong foot, fueling the arguments of those who said he was not his own man by traveling to Roosevelt's home at [Sagamore Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sagamore_Hill "Sagamore Hill") for advice on his acceptance speech, saying that he needed "the President's judgment and criticism".[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris529-74) Taft supported most of Roosevelt's policies. He argued that labor had a right to organize, but not boycott, and that corporations and the wealthy must also obey the law. Bryan wanted the railroads to be owned by the government, but Taft preferred that they remain in the private sector, with their maximum rates set by the [Interstate Commerce Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interstate_Commerce_Commission "Interstate Commerce Commission"), subject to [judicial review](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judicial_review "Judicial review"). Taft attributed blame for the recent recession, the [Panic of 1907](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panic_of_1907 "Panic of 1907"), to stock speculation and other abuses, and felt some reform of the currency (the U.S. was on the [gold standard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gold_standard "Gold standard")) was needed to allow flexibility in the government's response to poor economic times, that specific legislation on [trusts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trust_(business) "Trust (business)") was needed to supplement the [Sherman Antitrust Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sherman_Antitrust_Act "Sherman Antitrust Act"), and that [the constitution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Constitution_of_the_United_States "Constitution of the United States") should be amended to allow for an income tax, thus overruling decisions of the Supreme Court striking such a tax down. Roosevelt's expansive use of executive power had been controversial; Taft proposed to continue his policies, but place them on more solid legal underpinnings through the passage of legislation.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_197316%E2%80%9318-75)

Taft upset some progressives by choosing [Frank Harris Hitchcock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Harris_Hitchcock "Frank Harris Hitchcock") as chairman of the [Republican National Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_National_Committee "Republican National Committee") (RNC), placing him in charge of the presidential campaign. Hitchcock was quick to bring in men closely allied with big business.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_197345-76) Taft took an August vacation in [Hot Springs, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hot_Springs,_Virginia "Hot Springs, Virginia"), where he irritated political advisors by spending more time on golf than strategy. After seeing a newspaper photo of Taft taking a large swing at a golf ball, Roosevelt warned him against candid shots.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMorris524%E2%80%93525-77)

[![Image 15](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/ElectoralCollege1908.svg/330px-ElectoralCollege1908.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ElectoralCollege1908.svg)

1908 electoral vote results

Roosevelt, frustrated by his own relative inaction, showered Taft with advice, fearing that the electorate would not appreciate Taft's qualities, and that Bryan would win. Roosevelt's supporters spread rumors that the president was in effect running Taft's campaign. This annoyed Nellie Taft, who never trusted the Roosevelts.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1358%E2%80%93360-78) Nevertheless, Roosevelt supported the Republican nominee with such enthusiasm that humorists suggested "TAFT" stood for "Take advice from Theodore".[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie136-79)

Bryan urged a system of bank guarantees, so that depositors could be repaid if banks failed, but Taft opposed this, offering a [postal savings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Postal_savings "Postal savings") system instead.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_197315%E2%80%9316-73) The issue of prohibition of alcohol entered the campaign when in mid-September, [Carrie Nation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrie_Nation "Carrie Nation") called on Taft and demanded to know his views. Taft and Roosevelt had agreed the party platform would take no position on the matter, and Nation left indignant, to allege that Taft was irreligious and against temperance. Taft, at Roosevelt's advice, ignored the issue.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1374%E2%80%93376-80)

In the end, Taft won by a comfortable margin. Taft defeated Bryan by 321 electoral votes to 162; however, he garnered just 51.6 percent of the popular vote.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_197357-81) Nellie Taft said regarding the campaign, "There was nothing to criticize, except his not knowing or caring about the way the game of politics is played."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_197358-82) Longtime White House usher [Ike Hoover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ike_Hoover "Ike Hoover") recalled that Taft came often to see Roosevelt during the campaign, but seldom between the election and Inauguration Day, March 4, 1909.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_197319-83)

On February 18, 1909, after his election but before his inauguration, Taft was recognized as a [Mason at sight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mason_at_sight "Mason at sight") at the Scottish Rite Cathedral in Cincinnati.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-84)

## Presidency (1909–1913)

Main article: [Presidency of William Howard Taft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_William_Howard_Taft "Presidency of William Howard Taft")

### Inauguration and appointments

Further information: [Inauguration of William Howard Taft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inauguration_of_William_Howard_Taft "Inauguration of William Howard Taft")

[![Image 16](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Taft_inauguration.jpg/330px-Taft_inauguration.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Taft_inauguration.jpg)

1909 inauguration

Taft was [sworn in as president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inauguration_of_William_Howard_Taft "Inauguration of William Howard Taft") on March 4, 1909. Due to a winter storm that coated Washington with ice, Taft was inaugurated within the Senate Chamber rather than outside the Capitol as is customary. The new president stated in his inaugural address that he had been honored to have been "one of the advisers of my distinguished predecessor" and to have had a part "in the reforms he has initiated. I should be untrue to myself, to my promises, and to the declarations of the party platform on which I was elected if I did not make the maintenance and enforcement of those reforms a most important feature of my administration".[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1393%E2%80%93395-85) He pledged to make those reforms long-lasting, ensuring that honest businessmen did not suffer uncertainty through change of policy. He spoke of the need to reduce the 1897 Dingley tariff, of the need for antitrust reform, and for continued advancement of the Philippines toward full self-government.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1395-86) Roosevelt left office with regret that his tenure in the position he enjoyed so much was over and, to keep out of Taft's way, arranged for a year-long hunting trip to Africa.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_197345-87)

Soon after the Republican convention, Taft and Roosevelt had discussed which cabinet officers would stay on. Taft kept only [Agriculture Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agriculture_Secretary "Agriculture Secretary")[James Wilson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Wilson_(Iowa) "James Wilson (Iowa)") and Postmaster General [George von Lengerke Meyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_von_Lengerke_Meyer "George von Lengerke Meyer") (who was transferred to the Navy Department). Others appointed to the Taft cabinet included [Philander Knox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philander_Knox "Philander Knox"), who had served under McKinley and Roosevelt as Attorney General, as the new Secretary of State, and [Franklin MacVeagh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franklin_MacVeagh "Franklin MacVeagh") as [Treasury Secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Treasury_Secretary "Treasury Secretary").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_1383%E2%80%93387-88)[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_197350-89)

Taft did not enjoy the easy relationship with the press that Roosevelt had, choosing not to offer himself for interviews or photo opportunities as often as his predecessor had.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-american_chronicle-90) His administration marked a change in style from the charismatic leadership of Roosevelt to Taft's quieter passion for the rule of law.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_197360-91)

### First Lady's illness

Early in Taft's term, in May 1909, his wife Nellie had a severe [stroke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stroke "Stroke") that left her paralyzed in one arm and one leg and deprived her of the power of speech. Taft spent several hours each day looking after her and teaching her to speak again, which took a year.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTERosen_201861%E2%80%9362-92)

### Foreign policy

#### Organization and principles

[![Image 17](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e7/TAFT%2C_William_H-President_%28BEP_engraved_portrait%29.jpg/330px-TAFT%2C_William_H-President_%28BEP_engraved_portrait%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TAFT,_William_H-President_(BEP_engraved_portrait).jpg)

[](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:TAFT,_William_H-President_(BEP_engraved_portrait).jpg "File:TAFT, William H-President (BEP engraved portrait).jpg")

[BEP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bureau_of_Engraving_and_Printing "Bureau of Engraving and Printing") engraved portrait of Taft as President 

Taft made it a priority to restructure the [State Department](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_Department "State Department"), noting, "it is organized on the basis of the needs of the government in 1800 instead of 1900."[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_197368-93) The department was for the first time organized into geographical divisions, including desks for the Far East, Latin America and Western Europe.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_197371-94) The department's first in-service training program was established, and appointees spent a month in Washington before going to their posts.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEScholes_and_Scholes25-95) Taft and Secretary of State Knox had a strong relationship, and the president listened to his counsel on matters foreign and domestic. According to historian Paolo E. Coletta, Knox was not a good diplomat, and had poor relations with the Senate, press, and many foreign leaders, especially those from Latin America.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_1973183%E2%80%93185-96)

There was broad agreement between Taft and Knox on major foreign policy goals; the U.S. would not interfere in European affairs, and would use force if necessary to enforce the [Monroe Doctrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monroe_Doctrine "Monroe Doctrine") in the Americas. The defense of the Panama Canal, which was under construction throughout Taft's term (it opened in 1914), guided [United States foreign policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_foreign_policy "United States foreign policy") in the Caribbean and Central America. Previous administrations had made efforts to promote American business interests overseas, but Taft went a step further and used the web of American diplomats and consuls abroad to further trade. Such ties, Taft hoped, would promote world peace.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_1973183%E2%80%93185-96) Taft pushed for arbitration treaties with Great Britain and France, but the Senate was not willing to yield to arbitrators its constitutional prerogative to approve treaties.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_1973276%E2%80%93278-97)

#### Tariffs and reciprocity

[![Image 18](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/Howard_Taft%2C_bust_portrait%2C_facing_right_LCCN2005696045.jpg/250px-Howard_Taft%2C_bust_portrait%2C_facing_right_LCCN2005696045.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Howard_Taft,_bust_portrait,_facing_right_LCCN2005696045.jpg)

Taft in 1911

At the time of Taft's presidency, [protectionism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protectionism "Protectionism") through the use of tariffs was a fundamental position of the Republican Party.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTELurie102%E2%80%93103-98) The [Dingley Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dingley_Act "Dingley Act") tariff had been enacted to protect American industry from foreign competition. The 1908 party platform had supported unspecified revisions to the Dingley Act, and Taft interpreted this to mean reduction. Taft called a special session of Congress to convene on March 15, 1909, to deal with the tariff question.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_197356%E2%80%9358-99)

[Sereno E. Payne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sereno_E._Payne "Sereno E. Payne"), chairman of the [House Ways and Means Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_Ways_and_Means_Committee "House Ways and Means Committee"), had held hearings in late 1908, and sponsored the resulting draft legislation. On balance, the bill reduced tariffs slightly, but when it passed the House in April 1909 and reached the Senate, the chairman of the [Senate Finance Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Finance_Committee "Senate Finance Committee"), Rhode Island senator [Nelson W. Aldrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nelson_W._Aldrich "Nelson W. Aldrich"), attached many amendments raising rates. This outraged progressives such as Wisconsin's [Robert M. La Follette](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_M._La_Follette "Robert M. La Follette"), who urged Taft to say that the bill was not in accord with the party platform. Taft refused, angering them.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_197360%E2%80%9365-100) Taft insisted that most imports from the Philippines be free of duty, and according to Anderson, showed effective leadership on a subject he was knowledgeable on and cared about.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_1973102%E2%80%93108-101)

When opponents sought to modify the tariff bill to allow for an income tax, Taft opposed it on the ground that the Supreme Court would likely strike it down as unconstitutional, as it had before. Instead, they proposed a constitutional amendment, which passed both houses in early July, was sent to the states, and by 1913 was ratified as the [Sixteenth Amendment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sixteenth_Amendment_to_the_United_States_Constitution "Sixteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution"). In the [conference committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conference_committee "Conference committee"), Taft won some victories, such as limiting the tax on lumber. The conference report passed both houses, and Taft signed it on August 6, 1909. The [Payne-Aldrich tariff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Payne-Aldrich_tariff "Payne-Aldrich tariff") was immediately controversial. According to Coletta, "Taft had lost the initiative, and the wounds inflicted in the acrid tariff debate never healed".[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_197365%E2%80%9371-102)

[![Image 19](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/JackCanuckOYes.jpg/250px-JackCanuckOYes.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:JackCanuckOYes.jpg)

Newton McConnell cartoon showing Canadian suspicions that Taft and others were only interested in Canada when it was prosperous

In Taft's [annual message](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_of_the_Union "State of the Union") sent to Congress in December 1910, he urged a [free trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Free_trade "Free trade") accord with Canada. Britain at that time still handled Canada's foreign relations, and Taft found the British and Canadian governments willing. Many in Canada opposed an accord, fearing the U.S. would dump it when it became inconvenient, as it had the 1854 [Elgin-Marcy Treaty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elgin-Marcy_Treaty "Elgin-Marcy Treaty") in 1866, and farm and fisheries interests in the United States were also opposed. After talks with Canadian officials in January 1911, Taft had the agreement, which was not a treaty, introduced into Congress. It passed in late July. The [Parliament of Canada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parliament_of_Canada "Parliament of Canada") led by Prime Minister Sir [Wilfrid Laurier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilfrid_Laurier "Wilfrid Laurier") had deadlocked over the issue. Canadians turned Laurier out of office in the [September 1911 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1911_Canadian_federal_election "1911 Canadian federal election") and [Robert Borden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Borden "Robert Borden") became the new prime minister. No cross-border agreement was concluded, and the debate deepened divisions within the Republican Party.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_1973141%E2%80%93152-103)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEPringle_vol_2593%E2%80%93595-104)

#### Latin America

See also: [Dollar Diplomacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dollar_Diplomacy "Dollar Diplomacy")

Taft and his Secretary of State, Philander Knox, instituted a policy of [Dollar Diplomacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dollar_Diplomacy "Dollar Diplomacy") toward Latin America, believing U.S. investment would benefit all involved, while diminishing European influence in regions where the [Monroe Doctrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monroe_Doctrine "Monroe Doctrine") applied. The policy was unpopular among Latin American states that did not wish to become financial protectorates of the United States, as well as in the U.S. Senate, many of whose members believed the U.S. should not interfere abroad.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_1973185,_190-105) No foreign affairs controversy tested Taft's policy more than the collapse of the Mexican regime and subsequent turmoil of the [Mexican Revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Revolution "Mexican Revolution").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_1973271-106)

[![Image 20](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Presidents_Taft_and_Diaz%2C_Oct._1909.jpg/250px-Presidents_Taft_and_Diaz%2C_Oct._1909.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Presidents_Taft_and_Diaz,_Oct._1909.jpg)

Taft and [Porfirio Díaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porfirio_D%C3%ADaz "Porfirio Díaz"), Ciudad Juárez, Mexico, 1909

When Taft entered office, Mexico was increasingly restless under the grip of longtime dictator [Porfirio Díaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porfirio_D%C3%ADaz "Porfirio Díaz"). Many Mexicans backed his opponent, [Francisco Madero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_Madero "Francisco Madero").[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurton_200470-107) There were a number of incidents in which Mexican rebels crossed the U.S. border to obtain horses and weapons; Taft sought to prevent this by ordering the [U.S. Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U.S._Army "U.S. Army") to the border areas for maneuvers. Taft told his military aide, [Archibald Butt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archibald_Butt "Archibald Butt"), that "I am going to sit on the lid and it will take a great deal to pry me off".[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurton_200472-108) He showed his support for Díaz by meeting with him at [El Paso, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Paso,_Texas "El Paso, Texas"), and [Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciudad_Ju%C3%A1rez,_Chihuahua "Ciudad Juárez, Chihuahua"), the first meeting between a U.S. and a Mexican president and also the first time an American president visited Mexico.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarris20091%E2%80%932-109) The day of the summit, [Frederick Russell Burnham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frederick_Russell_Burnham "Frederick Russell Burnham") and a [Texas Ranger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Ranger_Division "Texas Ranger Division") captured and disarmed an assassin holding a [palm pistol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protector_Palm_Pistol "Protector Palm Pistol") only a few feet from the two presidents.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEHarris20091%E2%80%932-109) Before the election in Mexico, Díaz jailed opposition candidate [Francisco I. Madero](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francisco_I._Madero "Francisco I. Madero"), whose supporters took up arms. This resulted in both the ousting of Díaz and [a revolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mexican_Revolution "Mexican Revolution") that would continue for another ten years. In the U.S.'s [Arizona Territory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arizona_Territory "Arizona Territory"), two citizens were killed and almost a dozen injured, some as a result of gunfire across the border. Taft was against an aggressive response and so instructed the territorial governor.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_1973271-106)

Nicaragua's president, [José Santos Zelaya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Santos_Zelaya "José Santos Zelaya"), wanted to revoke commercial concessions granted to American companies,[[j]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-110) and American diplomats quietly favored rebel forces under [Juan Estrada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juan_Jos%C3%A9_Estrada "Juan José Estrada").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurton_200466%E2%80%9367-111) Nicaragua was in debt to foreign powers, and the U.S. was unwilling to let an alternate canal route fall into the hands of Europeans. Zelaya's elected successor, [José Madriz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jos%C3%A9_Madriz "José Madriz"), could not put down the rebellion as U.S. forces interfered, and in August 1910, the Estrada forces took [Managua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Managua "Managua"), the capital. The U.S. compelled Nicaragua to accept a loan, and sent officials to ensure it was repaid from government revenues. The country remained unstable, and after another coup in 1911 and more disturbances in 1912, Taft sent troops to begin the [United States occupation of Nicaragua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_occupation_of_Nicaragua "United States occupation of Nicaragua"), which lasted until 1933.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_1973187%E2%80%93190-112)[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEBurton_200467%E2%80%9369-113)

Treaties among Panama, Colombia, and the United States to resolve disputes arising from the Panamanian Revolution of 1903 had been signed by the lame-duck Roosevelt administration in early 1909, and were approved by the Senate and also ratified by Panama. Colombia, however, declined to ratify the treaties, and after the 1912 elections, Knox offered $10 million to the Colombians (later raised to $25 million). The Colombians felt the amount inadequate, and requested arbitration; the matter was not settled under the Taft administration.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEColetta_1973186%E2%80%93187-114)

#### East Asia

Due to his years in the Philippines, Taft was keenly interested as president in East Asian affairs.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEScholes_and_Scholes109-115) Taft considered relations with Europe relatively unimportant, but because of the potential for trade and investment, Taft ranked the post of minister to China as most important in the Foreign Service. Knox did not agree, and declined a suggestion that he go to [Peking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peking "Peking") to view the facts on the ground. Taft considered Roosevelt's minister there, [William W. Rockhill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_W._Rockhill "William W. Rockhill"), as uninterested in the China trade, and replaced him with [William J. Calhoun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_J._Calhoun "William J. Calhoun"), whom McKinley and Roosevelt had sent on several foreign missions. Knox did not listen to Calhoun on policy, and there were often conflicts.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEScholes_and_Scholes21%E2%80%9323-116) Taft and Knox tried unsuccessfully to extend John Hay's [Open Door Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_Door_Policy "Open Door Policy") to [Manchuria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchuria "Manchuria").[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Howard_Taft#cite_note-FOOTNOTEAnderson_1973250%E2%80%93255-117)

In 1898, an American company had gained a concession for a railroad between [Hankow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hankow "Hankow") and [Sichuan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sichuan "Sichuan"), but the Chinese revoked the agreement in 1904 after the company (which was indemnified for the revocation) breached the agreement by selling a majority stake outside the United States. The Chinese imperial government got the money for the indemnity from the British Hong Kong government, on condition British subjects would be favored if foreign capital was needed to build the railroad line, and in 1909, a British-led consortium began negotiations.[[108]]
